name: Briar Patel
life: “I still remember the coat my son wore to plead for a second chance.” Monday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Briar stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: My son needs a good shirt for court. I asked the volunteer if the stranger might lend it.
appearance: Briar has a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow, a small notch in the left eyebrow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a sand-colored linen shirt. It usually goes with a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. When somebody else has the floor, Briar touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word.
personality: Briar enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To borrow a respectable shirt for court with permission.
family: Leon Armas is Briar’s second cousin. Briar gets to change the plan. Leon offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *A chair on the quay*, Leon says, “Everybody wants a retirement speech. He wants his granddaughter admitted past the gate for ten minutes.”
connections: Lola Vidal. Borrowing a court shirt depends on knowing the person who actually runs the linen round.

reactions.situation: An elderly tenant wants to iron the collar personally
reactions.response: Briar lets the tenant do the collar at a safe height and takes the heavier laundry.
